note: Underline the first occurrence of each term per explanation; match case-insensitively on whole words. Translate per locale.

terms.ACK: Acknowledgment: tells the sender which bytes (TCP) or packets (QUIC) have arrived.
terms.ARP: Address Resolution Protocol: finds the MAC address that owns an IPv4 address on the local network.
terms.AEAD: Authenticated encryption: encrypts data and adds a tag that proves it wasn't altered.
terms.ALPN: Application-Layer Protocol Negotiation: TLS extension where client and server agree on h2, h3, etc.
terms.Broadcast: A frame or packet addressed to every device on the local network.
terms.CA: Certificate Authority: an organisation browsers trust to vouch for a server's name and key.
terms.CCMP: The AES-based encryption and integrity method used by WPA2/WPA3 Wi-Fi.
terms.Checksum: A small value computed over data so the receiver can detect corruption.
terms.DAD: Duplicate Address Detection: IPv6 check that nobody else uses an address before taking it.
terms.DNSSEC: DNS Security Extensions: digital signatures that prove DNS answers weren't forged.
terms.DoH: DNS over HTTPS: DNS questions and answers carried inside an encrypted HTTPS connection.
terms.ECH: Encrypted Client Hello: hides the server name (SNI) during the TLS handshake.
terms.EDNS: Extension mechanisms for DNS: an OPT record that allows larger messages and flags like DO.
terms.FIN: TCP flag meaning 'I have no more data to send'.
terms.Handshake: The opening exchange in which two sides agree on parameters before sending data.
terms.Hop limit: IPv6's version of TTL: decremented by each router; at zero the packet is dropped.
terms.Lease: How long a DHCP-assigned address may be used before it must be renewed.
terms.MAC address: A 48-bit hardware address used to deliver frames on the local network.
terms.MSS: Maximum Segment Size: the largest chunk of data TCP puts in one segment, usually 1,460 bytes.
terms.MTU: Maximum Transmission Unit: the largest packet a link carries, 1,500 bytes on Ethernet.
terms.MX: Mail exchanger: DNS record naming the servers that accept mail for a domain.
terms.NAT: Network Address Translation: a router rewrites private addresses to its public one.
terms.Nonce: A random number used once, so each handshake produces fresh keys.
terms.Port: A number that picks which program on a host receives the data.
terms.PTK: Pairwise Transient Key: the per-session Wi-Fi key derived in the 4-way handshake.
terms.QUIC: A transport protocol over UDP with TLS 1.3 built in; the basis of HTTP/3.
terms.RRSIG: A DNSSEC signature over a set of DNS records.
terms.RTT: Round-trip time: how long a message takes to reach the other side and come back.
terms.SACK: Selective acknowledgment: TCP option that reports data received after a gap.
terms.SAE: Simultaneous Authentication of Equals: WPA3's password-based key exchange.
terms.Segment: One TCP packet's worth of data.
terms.SLAAC: Stateless address auto-configuration: an IPv6 host builds its own address from the router's prefix.
terms.SNI: Server Name Indication: the site name sent in the TLS Client Hello.
terms.SSID: The name of a Wi-Fi network.
terms.Stream: An independent ordered flow of data inside one QUIC or HTTP/2 connection.
terms.SYN: TCP flag that opens a connection and sets the starting sequence number.
terms.TLS: Transport Layer Security: encrypts and authenticates a connection.
terms.TTL: Time to live: decremented by each router; at zero the packet is dropped. In DNS, how long an answer may be cached.
terms.UDP: User Datagram Protocol: sends independent datagrams with no handshake or resends.
terms.Upgrade: HTTP header asking to switch the connection to another protocol, such as WebSocket.
